programs.name: YLRL Ethel Smith K4LMB Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: $2,500 for a licensed female amateur radio operator seeking a Bachelor's or Graduate degree full time at an accredited college or university. There are no residency restrictions and non-US amateurs are eligible. YLRL membership and a communications, radio or electronics course of study are both preferences, not bars.

amount.awardCountRaw: Not published. The page names three scholarships and states an amount for each; it states no award count.

deadline.note: The captured page publishes no opening date and no deadline anywhere. It describes the three scholarships and points at the YLRL apply page for the current opening and deadline dates. Deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed.

constraints.rawText: Applicant must be female.
Applicant must have an Amateur Radio License. There are no residency restrictions. Non-U.S. Amateurs are eligible.

The Ethel Smith, K4LMB and Mary Lou Brown, NM7N scholarships are intended for full-time students. For these scholarships, applicants must intend to seek a Bachelor's or Graduate degree from an accredited college or university.
Preference will be given to students studying communications, radio, electronics, or Amateur Radio related arts and sciences.

fields: Amateur Radio related arts and sciences

constraints.rawText: Preference will be given to YLRL members.

spec.note: YLRL membership is a preference, not a bar.

programs.rawOtherText: One of only two verified non-ARRL US ham scholarship application paths; its intake does not run through the ARRL catalog. Every fact in this record is quoted from fixtures/ylrl/00-ylrl-net-scholarships.html. Status is `unknown` rather than `open` because the page states no cycle at all: an unpublished deadline cannot support an open badge.

programs.name: YLRL Marte Wessel K0EPE Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: $1,500 for a licensed female amateur radio operator studying part time at an accredited educational institution while working full time. Stay-at-home parents and caregivers count as full-time work, and high-school students are exempt from the work requirement. Any accredited technical or vocational school and any two- or four-year college qualifies.

deadline.note: The captured page publishes no opening date and no deadline anywhere. It points at the YLRL apply page for the current opening and deadline dates. Deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed.

constraints.rawText: Applicant must be female.
Applicant must have an Amateur Radio License. There are no residency restrictions. Non-U.S. Amateurs are eligible.
Qualifying educational institutions/programs include: Any accredited technical or vocational school. A two or four year college or university.

The Martha “Marte” Wessel, K0EPE scholarship is intended for a part-time student of an accredited educational institution who is working full-time. Full time work includes a stay-at-home parent or caregiver. High School students are exempt from the full-time work requirement.

spec.note: Aimed at a part-time student working full time; stay-at-home parents and caregivers count, and high-school students are exempt from the work requirement.

constraints.rawText: Preference will be given to students studying communications, radio, electronics, or Amateur Radio related arts and sciences.

fields: Amateur Radio related arts and sciences

constraints.rawText: Preference will be given to YLRL members.

spec.note: YLRL membership is a preference, not a bar.

programs.rawOtherText: The one award in this corpus written FOR part-time students. partTimeOK is true and degreeLevels is empty on purpose: YLRL restricts neither, and an empty allow-list here means the funder set no level, not that no level qualifies.

NAME CAVEAT: the club's rebuilt page is headed "Club Scholarships" and names no individual award; "Copeland" comes from the 2026-08-02 research pass and could not be re-confirmed against the capture. amount.amountRaw: Not published. There is not a single dollar figure on the club's scholarships page. Do not infer an amount.

deadline.note: RECUR annual_window tz=America/Chicago window=05-01..07-31 | Applications open May 1 and close July 31 each year. programs.name: Yasme Foundation Supporting Grants
programs.summary: Board-selected support for youth programmes, developing-country radio societies, Reverse Beacon Network nodes and other foundations' scholarship funds; the companion Yasme Excellence Award is recognition on the same board-initiated basis. Observed awards run $5,000 to $7,500. There is no application form, no portal and no deadline.

amount.amountRaw: $5,000 to $7,500 observed. Yasme publishes no award schedule; these are the figures the 2026-08-02 research pass observed in announcements.

deadline.note: There is no application and no deadline. The board initiates awards and announces them retrospectively, roughly twice a year. The practical route is to be visible: publish your work and let the board find it.

constraints.rawText: Awards are board-initiated. There is no application process.

programs.rawOtherText: yasme.org 301s /feed/ and /wp-json/ to a 403 page for non-browser clients, so GrantSpotter does not poll it and no capture of that site exists in this repository. We do not spoof a browser user agent to defeat a deliberate access policy; Yasme announcements are relayed by the ARRL news RSS feed, which is what the change detector watches instead. NOT ASSERTED HERE: a reporting obligation. Earlier drafts stated one for recipients of the associated YASME scholarship, but with no fetchable page there is no funder sentence to quote, and an obligation with a fabricated citation is worse than an unstated one.

programs.name: NCDXF Grant Program
programs.summary: Cash grants to individuals and groups who use amateur radio to advance education, science and international goodwill. In practice the recipients are well-designed DXpeditions to locations high on the most-wanted lists, so this is not a collegiate programme. Applicants must have a significant financial stake of their own.

amount.amountRaw: Not published. The guidelines page states no amount, no cap and no total; it distinguishes only "major support" for expeditions to the most-wanted locations from "a smaller amount of support" for other projects.

deadline.note: Rolling: the guidelines page publishes no deadline of any kind. NCDXF's own instruction is to allow lead time, because the entire Board of Directors reviews each application — normally you should allow two months lead time for action.

programs.applyContact: Applications must be made by completing (1) a Budget Worksheet and (2) an Application Form, and submitting both to NCDXF.

constraints.rawText: A basic philosophy of the NCDXF is that expedition participants themselves should have a significant financial stake in their expedition and that the expedition should be likely to proceed even without financial support from the NCDXF.

spec.note: The applicant must carry a significant financial stake; NCDXF does not fund the whole cost.

constraints.rawText: The Northern California DX Foundation (NCDXF) is a US non-profit organization which provides financial support to individuals and groups who use amateur radio communications to advance and promote education, science and international goodwill.

spec.note: The project must advance education, science or international goodwill through amateur radio.

constraints.rawText: The NCDXF encourages applicants to be active financial contributors to the Foundation.

spec.note: Being an active financial contributor to NCDXF is encouraged.

fundingRestrictions: With the exception of excess baggage charges, we do not consider commercially available transportation costs when we are working on a grant request approval.

Expeditions to unusual locations as defined by the Islands on the Air (IOTA) program, Grid Square awards and various radio contests are not supported unless the support can be justified without reference to these activities.

costShareRequired.quote: A basic philosophy of the NCDXF is that expedition participants themselves should have a significant financial stake in their expedition and that the expedition should be likely to proceed even without financial support from the NCDXF.

programs.rawOtherText: ncdxf.org returns 403 for both robots.txt and sitemap.xml, so this record is re-verified by hand each quarter rather than crawled aggressively. NOT ASSERTED HERE: the "roughly $1.2M distributed over about 48 years" figure from the 2026-08-02 research pass, which appears nowhere on the captured guidelines page and is therefore not published as an amount. NOT ASSERTED HERE either: an emailed intake to a treasurer — the word "treasurer" appears zero times on the page, whose own instruction is to complete a Budget Worksheet and an Application Form and submit both to NCDXF.

programs.name: NCDXF W6EEN Memorial Scholarship
programs.summary: Full tuition at any DX University or Contest University session held in North America, for licensed amateurs aged 25 or younger. There is no restriction as to class of license. No dollar figure is published because the award is the course itself, and an eligible ham applies by contacting the university directly rather than NCDXF.

amount.amountRaw: Full tuition at DX University or Contest University sessions held in North America. No dollar figure is published.

deadline.note: No deadline is published. Availability tracks the DX University and Contest University session schedules, which NCDXF does not restate on this page.

constraints.rawText: If you are a licensed amateur radio operator 25 years of age or younger, you can apply for a free tuition scholarship by contacting the appropriate University directly.
There is no restriction as to class of license.

programs.rawOtherText: The page's apply instruction is to contact DX University or Contest University directly; NCDXF publishes their contact pages and does not take the application itself. "There is no restriction as to class of license" means ANY CLASS QUALIFIES — a floor of TECH — and never "no licence needed": the same sentence begins "If you are a licensed amateur radio operator". The page also carries a Previous ARRL Foundation Scholarship Program table marked No Longer Active; those rows are history, not an open award.

programs.name: SARA Student and Teacher Project Grants
programs.summary: The Society of Amateur Radio Astronomers funds student radio-astronomy projects in several small grants of no more than $200 each, or more with the approval of the grant committee. Teachers are now eligible too. Preference goes to students from fifth grade through college and to new and innovative ideas, and the application is a Word or PDF form emailed back to SARA.

amount.amountRaw: The funds will be divided up into several small grants of no more than $200 each or more, with the approval of the grant committee, to ensure that the money reaches the largest number of students. A ceiling with explicit committee discretion above it, so no maximum is asserted.

deadline.note: Rolling. No deadline of any kind appears anywhere on the grants page.

programs.applyContact: Email the completed form to grants at radio-astronomy.org

constraints.rawText: Preference will be given to students 5th grade through college and to new and innovative ideas.
UPDATE: Teachers are now eligible to apply for grants to bring radio astronomy to the classroom.

spec.note: Teachers became eligible by a later update line on the same page.

programs.rawOtherText: THE FIFTH-GRADE-THROUGH-COLLEGE RULE IS A PREFERENCE, NOT A BAR — the page's own word is "Preference" — so this constraint is soft and cannot exclude anybody. THE AWARD IS CASH, not a kit: the page says SARA "provides funds" and that the aim is that "the money reaches the largest number of students". Radio JOVE, SuperSID and INSPIRE appear on that page only as example projects an applicant might BUILD with the money, never as what SARA hands over; klass stays equipment_in_kind to match the source module's browse category, and the instrument is cash_range, which is what the page describes. The address is written "grants at radio-astronomy.org" here because that is how the page spells it, as an anti-spam measure. NOT ASSERTED HERE: a $500 outlier award, and an explicit welcome to international applicants — neither appears on the captured page.

programs.name: Radio Club of America Scholarship Program
programs.summary: Sixteen named funds, the Rappaport, Carr and Cooper awards among them, for undergraduate and graduate students on a wireless career track. An amateur licence is NOT required. Only students at roughly nine participating schools are eligible and the university selects the recipients, so a student never applies to RCA: the action is to ask your department whether your school participates.

amount.amountRaw: Per-award amounts are not published. About $15,000 a year is distributed in total, per the 2026-08-02 research pass.
amount.awardCountRaw: Not published; awards are distributed each May.

deadline.note: No deadline is published. Awards are distributed each May, and the timeline is set by the participating university rather than by RCA. If your school participates, ask your department for its internal date.

constraints.rawText: Only students at roughly nine participating schools are eligible, and the university selects the recipients. Students do not apply to the Radio Club of America directly.

spec.note: The institution nominates; no student-facing application exists.

constraints.rawText: Undergraduate and graduate students on a wireless career track. A ham licence is NOT required.

programs.rawOtherText: RCA runs on ClubExpress: sitemap.xml 403s, pretty URLs 404, and only content.aspx query-string URLs resolve — and the module id inside them changes without notice whenever RCA renumbers a module. That is why this record is curated by hand and re-verified quarterly rather than crawled, and why applyUrl is the club's root rather than a deep link that breaks silently. The wireless-track constraint is SOFT on purpose: it is our research on an unfetchable page, and a hard field bar built on that would exclude students RCA might well fund.
